questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Designing Application Architecture”?
options: Designing Application Architecture should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Designing Application Architecture helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Designing Application Architecture means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Designing Application Architecture removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Designing Application Architecture helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Designing Application Architecture is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Organizing features” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Organizing features” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Organizing features” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Organizing features” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Organizing features” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Organizing features” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Organizing features” under Designing Application Architecture. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Designing Application Architecture”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
